solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Didn't shut reference book writer has gone into

indicators.note: one thing having gone into another means it now sits inside it

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary, the classic reference book
a pen is a writing instrument, so a writer

explanation.surface: An unfinished sentence about an author who has disappeared into a reference work, with something left unclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unshut has been unclosed, a straightforward past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Jamaican town or ancient city in China

indicators.note: one piece set in another means it goes inside it

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, so china is a pal
Troy is the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: A quiz-style choice between a Caribbean town and an old Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Royal is a historic town near Kingston in Jamaica, once a notorious pirate haven.

clue.text: Item of lingerie at hand, with lace on the bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece on the bottom comes after the first one

parts.note: something at hand is near, or nigh
to lace a shoe is to tie it

explanation.surface: A description of a piece of underwear, close by, trimmed with lace along the hem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lace' seems a fabric but is the verb, to tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress, worn in bed, counts as an item of lingerie.

clue.text: Oz heroine briefly making a point

indicators.note: a name used briefly is cut down to its familiar short form

parts.note: Dorothy is the heroine of The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: A girl from The Wizard of Oz making a point in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' turns DOROTHY into its pet form DOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a small round mark, a point, as in a full stop or decimal point.

clue.text: Worrying about noise recurring in Alcatraz, say

indicators.note: set in one piece means placed inside it

parts.note: Alcatraz is an example of a prison, slang the can
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: something recurring runs back on itself, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Anxiety about a repeated din inside the famous island prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Alcatraz is the former island prison in San Francisco Bay; 'can' is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worn down by anxieties is to be fretful, a loose adjectival match.

clue.text: Hymn about Jesus almost over?

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters run backwards
almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Jesus is called the Lord

explanation.surface: A question whether a religious song about Christ is nearly done.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas carol is a festive religious song, a kind of hymn.

clue.text: Keen to study ditty we composed

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eager to look over a little song that we wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, quick-thinking mind is keen, so quick-witted equals keen.

clue.text: Shoot the breeze principally? One might

parts.note: a breeze is a wind, and principally puts it in the leading place
to bag game is to shoot it

explanation.surface: A question whether chatting idly is the main point, answered that someone could.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot the breeze' reads as idle chat, but is BAG + WIND, with 'principally' putting WIND first. The definition points back: one might shoot the breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome talker who never stops chattering would indeed shoot the breeze.

clue.text: Govern Niger after revolution

indicators.note: after a revolution things are overturned and reordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ruling the West African country once the uprising is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' rearranges NIGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as monarch, a direct synonym for govern.

clue.text: Car judge reversed across street

indicators.note: one piece lying across another spans it, holding it inside
the word is read backwards

parts.note: to regard something is to judge or consider it

explanation.surface: A vehicle and a magistrate driving the wrong way over a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragster is a specially built car for drag racing over a short straight track.

clue.text: Place to meet in 'ackney? That is relative

indicators.note: a Hackney Cockney drops the H, as the apostrophe shows

parts.note: a haunt is a regular meeting place
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Cockney asking about a meeting place in Hackney, then a remark that it is all relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is an East London borough; Cockneys there traditionally drop their aitches, so HAUNT loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a family relation, and auntie is the familiar form.

clue.text: Book in its entirety produced on time, in fact

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another follows it

parts.note: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament
wholly, fully

explanation.surface: A complete book delivered on schedule, as a matter of fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking honestly is saying what is in fact so; both phrases mean really.

clue.text: Bit of a fiddle? Suspect council of guilt

parts.note: to finger someone is to point to them as the suspect
a board is a governing council

explanation.surface: A fraud in the town hall, with suspicion falling on the council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like a swindle, but it is the violin. 'of guilt' completes the sense: to finger is to suspect of guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip on a violin's neck where strings are pressed is a part of the instrument.

clue.text: Sound of gunfire from urban guerrillas

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within these words

explanation.surface: A noise of shooting coming from city rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters inside 'urBAN Guerrillas'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud explosive report, as a gun makes when fired.

clue.text: Mentioned a bit of a fork in river

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word is as it is said

parts.note: a tine is a prong of a fork

explanation.surface: Someone mentioned part of a piece of cutlery lying in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyne is the river at Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyne is an English waterway in the north-east, flowing through Newcastle.

clue.text: Playing tonight — Man City

indicators.note: letters playing about are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A football fixture announcement: Manchester City are playing this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man City' looks like the football club, but 'Man' joins the fodder and 'City' is the definition. 'Playing' rearranges TONIGHT + MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottingham is an English city in the East Midlands.

clue.text: Finish off next article

indicators.note: to finish off a word is to remove its end

parts.note: then means next, after that

explanation.surface: An instruction to complete the following written piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of writing, but it is the grammatical one. 'Finish off' drops the last letter of THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the definite article is the commonest determiner in English.

clue.text: A funny programme and last parts of The Professionals, in no set order

parts.note: a sitcom is a situation comedy, a funny television programme

indicators.note: the last letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A comedy show and the closing scenes of the 1970s TV action series The Professionals, shown in random order.
explanation.walkthrough: The Professionals was a British TV crime drama. 'last parts of' takes E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking things just as they arrive means in random sequence, an idiomatic match.

clue.text: Cheers a military officer seizing large city of old

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of and holding within

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
Thebes was an ancient city, in Egypt or Greece

explanation.surface: A toast, and an army officer capturing an ancient metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like a drinking toast, but as an informal farewell it matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal sign-offs, wishing someone well on parting.

clue.text: Closed faulty power line

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed

indicators.note: a faulty arrangement is a wrong one, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A broken electricity cable has been shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power line' reads as a cable, but 'line' alone is the definition. 'faulty' rearranges POWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope used for hauling a vehicle is a kind of line.

clue.text: Fancy wife and that man getting together

parts.note: him refers to that man

explanation.surface: A romance: a wife and a man coming together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an attraction to someone, but is the noun meaning a passing notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden impulse or caprice is a fancy, a direct synonym.

clue.text: We act oddly, note, in cave!

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are kept

parts.note: a chit is a short note

explanation.surface: We behave strangely and leave a message inside a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave!' is Latin for beware, as British schoolboys used it as a warning; it looks like a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: Both cry beware, a warning to take care.

clue.text: Farm animal eats hot dog

indicators.note: eating takes something inside

parts.note: a cow is a farm animal
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A beast on a farm devours a hot dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot dog' reads as a sausage, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: The chow chow is a Chinese breed of dog with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Takes charge of macho publicity?

parts.note: he-, as in he-man, means macho or male
ads are advertisements, publicity

explanation.surface: A question whether someone leads a campaign of manly advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: HE as in he-man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads a team or department is in charge of it.

clue.text: Lolly: endlessly gooey snack item

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money, as is bread

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: sticky means gooey

explanation.surface: An ice lolly that has gone sticky, beside a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lolly' looks like a sweet on a stick, but is the slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin crisp stick of baked dough is eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Half-decent Queen record

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, the back half here

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen

explanation.surface: A record by the rock band Queen that is only moderately good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-' keeps the back half of DECENT, ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to record it, as in a ledger or log.

clue.text: To the west, a space in which to create temple

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading from right to left
a space in which something goes holds it inside

parts.note: a gap is a space
to do is to make or create

explanation.surface: Directions to a space out west for building a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts DO into A GAP, giving ADOGAP; 'To the west' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu place of worship.

clue.text: Little fellow's to hitchhike, covering miles

indicators.note: covering a thing goes around it, holding it inside

parts.note: to thumb a lift is to hitchhike

explanation.surface: A small man means to thumb a lift and travel many miles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Thumb is the folk-tale figure no bigger than a thumb, a tiny man.

clue.text: Minutes accepted at the start by old chairman

indicators.note: only the opening letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: Meeting minutes approved first thing by a former chairman.
explanation.walkthrough: Chairman Mao, the Chinese Communist leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Mao Zedong was Chinese Communist leader, known as Chairman of the party.

clue.text: Note enclosed by a person posting letter

indicators.note: the note sits inside, enclosed

parts.note: someone posting a letter is its sender
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A note tucked into an envelope by someone mailing a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like mail, but is an alphabet character. 'enclosed by' puts C into A SENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography, b, d, h and similar characters have strokes rising above the x-height.

clue.text: Dim-witted baronet stuck in river

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A slow-witted aristocrat stuck in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, the figurative sense of blunt.
